comment: Prof. Szymanska sets high expectations for a 100-level gen ed course, ideal for students with an interest in art history. The workload includes readings and papers, but her articulate teaching and thoughtful feedback enhance the learning experience. While accessible outside class, email responses are usually pretty delayed. Overall, decent class.

This professor expects their students to know how to write about art. She doesn't provide a clear foundation of what she's looking for when it comes to writing assignments. Instead, she simply asks her students to refer to examples she found on the internet. She seeks a writing style that simply hasn't been taught to most of us.

I'm sure she's nice outside of class, but if you are not one of her (few) favorite students, you are screwed. She's knowledgeable but grades fully off of the opinion she has of you. Her grading is not consistent and she won't grade anything until the last minute. This class had absolutely no business being this hard.
Prof. Szymanska's art survey is a great class. Very little homework, just intermittent papers and some annoying out of class things. Overall great class and great for history credit.
class can be boring at times, but overall she's an amazing teacher who cares about her students. Make sure not to ask stupid questions though.

Professor Szymanska is truly incredible. She is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the content she teaches. She is always available for help outside of class. I would love to take another class with her. She cares a lot about her students and wants them to do well. She is honestly such an inspiration and also has the cutest dog ever.

Dr. Szymanska is a professor I really look up to, even after just having her once freshman year. She makes herself widely accesible & is always there to help her students. She really cares about what you tell her & she will remember. Her class was incredible, its clear how much she knows & how much she really wants to share it with her students.

Very caring for her students and interested in what she teaches. Participation really matters. Weekly textbook readings and short writing assignments. Midterm and final involve a lot of memorization. Big VMFA project throughout the semester which is more difficult but go to her office hours and you will be fine. Not the easiest history gen ed.

Professor Szymanska really cares about the artwork and content in the class. Every class is a lecture but student participation really matters in the outcome of your grade. The midterm and final assessments are very detailed and cover a large amount of content so be prepared to memorize dates and facts about each artwork.
Lots of reading, but that is expected with advanced seminars and art history in general. She is very sweet and is interested in hearing what we all have to say.

Homeworks are textbook readings with a multiple choice for each chapter. You can get by doing the multiple choice and skimming readings, but you need to talk during class. Counts attendance and gives real participation grades so you need to participate. Short writing assignments every week (completion) and two exams that are easy if you study.

Dr. Szymanska is a truly amazing professor and genuinely cares about what she teaches. If you put effort into the class and engage with the material, you will do well. There is a lot of reading, and most are discussed in class, but she is pretty lax about group discussion and loves listening to student ideas. Come prepared & you'll be fine.

Every week there is a reading that is like 50-100 pages. For those readings there is a one page writing assignment. She also tries to not use Blackboard for the life of her and will try other platforms like canvas. During discussions she can be overly passive aggressive towards students. She can't make the class interesting so I never truly learned

She is sweet and enthusiastic about the topics, you can see that she truly cares and that makes the class engaging. She loves when students connect to the material and really tries to make the class enjoy what they are learning about. Articles assigned can be VERY long and are better to skim than read the entire thing. Not too hard of a grader.
